newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up, off highs, as Dow falters.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up, off highs, as Dow falters.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Friday, propelled by a rise in bond prices on expectations of European interest rate cuts, but the bourse retreated from its best levels on Wall Street's weak performance in early trade.

"The prospect of European interest rate cuts right now is much more important for the bourse than the wavering on Wall Street, which is holding up rather well considering the levels," a trader said. The Dow was hovering around 6,000 points.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 10.81 points or 0.5 percent at 2,162.43, while the CAC-40 October futures contract rose 6.5 points to 2,163.50.
* Volume was a brisk 4.7 billion francs.
* Even if the Bundesbank does not cut its rates, analysts say the Bank of France has scope to trim rates to bring them closer in line to German rates.

* Chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc closed up 3.16 percent at 147 francs after announcing a bigger than expected 13 percent rise in third quarter profit and said the increase would have been 25 percent if it weren't for a product recall. Some analysts were considering raising their earnings forecasts.
* Shares in Cie Generale des Eaux rose 2.48 percent to 619 francs.
Portfolio managers said chairman Jean-Marie Messier confirmed at a breakfast meeting that 1997 results would be sharply higher and relayed "a very confident message".

* Elf-Aquitaine finished unchanged at 420.50 francs and Total rose 0.42 percent to 407.20 francs. Brokerage SBC Warburg lowered its ratings on shares in both companies to 'hold' from 'buy', citing their recent gains.

* Axa rose 2.17 percent to 310 francs after brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu put the insurer on its list of recommended shares, citing its strong growth prospects, international presence and clean balance sheet.
* Cap Gemini Sogeti rose 12.50 francs to 251.80 after Daimler-Benz's Debis reiterated its interest in raising its stake from the current 24.4 percent.

* Lagardere, which rose 32 percent after the government chose its bid for Thomson SA, closed down 2.35 percent at 166 francs on profit-taking fueled by a political outcry and Finance Minister Jean Arthuis' remarks that the group would end the year with 28 billion francs of debt.
* Shares in Renault fell one percent to 118.70 francs on a newspaper report that raised concerns about its future plans to build truck motors with Germany's MAN.
